answers.answer: 1. Each player starts with 25 money. 2. Each player has 1 active association worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers lying on the reserve spaces. 3. Draw 8 Zoo cards, keep 4 and discard 4 face up. 4. Draw 2 Final Scoring cards and keep them hidden. 5. Put Action card Animals under the leftmost slot (strength 1); place the other four randomly in the remaining slots, all side I up. 6. Starting appeal positions are staggered by turn order: first player 0, second 1, third 2, fourth 3.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C–F: 25 money; 1 active and 3 inactive workers; draw 8/keep 4; draw 2 Final Scoring cards; Animals leftmost; appeal staggered by turn order.

answers.answer: 1. In a 4-player game, place 4 Base Conservation Projects face up below the Association board; in 2- or 3-player games, place 3. 2. In a 2-player game only, block the left level of the left project, middle level of the middle project, right level of the right project, and the three donation spaces in the donation area's left column; these spaces are unavailable to both players. 3. With 3 or 4 players, no project levels or donation spaces are blocked at setup. 4. Reveal the six display cards after every player has chosen their starting hand cards.
answers.evidence: Setup 5b–5c: four projects in a 4-player game, otherwise three; 2-player-only blocking; Setup G: reveal display after hand selection.

answers.answer: 1. After using the card in slot 4, remove it; shift all cards left of the empty slot one place right, then put the used card in slot 1. 2. Set action strength before beginning the action. Each X-token spent adds 1 strength and returns to supply; X-tokens gained during the action cannot boost that action. 3. You may hold at most 5 X-tokens. 4. Resolve an ‘after finishing’ effect only after completing the action, moving the used Action card, and then perform that effect.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: remove the card, shift cards left of its slot right, put it in slot 1; X-token strength is set before the action; ‘After finishing’ effects follow action-card movement.

answers.answer: 1. You may not take a regular action that plays zero animals or builds zero buildings; you may not do nothing. 2. Instead, choose the X-token alternative: select an Action card, move it to slot 1 with normal card shifting, and take exactly 1 X-token. The card's strength and upgrade side do not matter. 3. You cannot take this alternative while holding 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and X-TOKEN action: ‘You may not do nothing’; alternative takes exactly one X-token and cannot be used at the five-token limit.

answers.answer: 1. When the Break token reaches the last space, ignore any further movement beyond that space and give the player who reached it 1 X-token. 2. The triggering player finishes the current turn; the break occurs after that turn. 3. The next turn is the next player's turn clockwise after the break procedure. 4. A break triggered during the turn does not interrupt the remaining action or turn.
answers.evidence: Break track: ‘break takes place after the end of your current turn’; gain 1 X-token; ignore steps beyond last space.

answers.answer: 1. Cards I advances the Break token 2 spaces, then either draws from the deck according to its strength table (maximum 3 cards, with any required discard) or, at strength 5+, snaps exactly 1 display card of your choice regardless of reputation and takes no deck cards. 2. Cards II also advances the Break token 2 spaces, then draws from the deck and/or display cards within reputation range in any order using its improved table; at strength 5 the example is 4 cards drawn and 1 discarded. Its snap option takes exactly 1 display card beginning at strength 3, ignores reputation, and does not include a deck draw. 3. Reputation range limits only the Cards II display-draw option, not snapping. 4. Cards taken from the display are replenished at the end of your turn. 5. There is no in-turn hand limit; discard down to your hand limit at breaks.
answers.evidence: CARDS action: both sides advance Break token 2; Side I snap at 5+; Side II snap from 3; display not replenished until turn complete; hand limit only at breaks.

answers.answer: 1. ‘Within reputation range’ means the display card in the folder matching your Reputation counter and every lower-numbered folder. 2. Reputation 10 and above requires the upgraded Cards action. 3. At reputation 15, each further reputation step gives 1 appeal instead. 4. You may not inspect the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: Reputation track and display: range definition, reputation 10+ requires Cards II, overflow at 15 converts to appeal; discard pile may not be viewed.

answers.answer: 1. Build I builds exactly 1 building of size no greater than strength; Build II builds any number of different buildings whose total size does not exceed strength, but never two identical buildings in one action. 2. Buildings cost 2 money per space, paid before placing each building. 3. Your first building must cover at least one border space; later buildings must touch an existing building by at least one edge. 4. Build only on empty spaces; do not extend off-map, overlap buildings, or cover water/rock. Restricted-icon spaces require Build II. 5. A kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. 6. Each pavilion immediately and once increases appeal by 1.
answers.evidence: BUILD action and placement rules: I/II limits and cost; first building border placement; later adjacency; restricted spaces; kiosk spacing; pavilion appeal.

answers.answer: 1. Build I can build kiosks, pavilions, standard enclosures, and one Petting Zoo per zoo (size 3); the Petting Zoo is available on side I. 2. Build II additionally permits Reptile Houses and Large Bird Aviaries (each size 5, one of each type per zoo) and permits restricted-icon map spaces. 3. The supply contains four tiles of each special enclosure type, one for each of four players. 4. The Build action cannot build unique buildings; those enter play through Sponsor cards. 5. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately grants 7 appeal, regardless of what effect covered the spaces.
answers.evidence: Buildings available through Build table and Side II: one each special enclosure; four tiles of each; unique buildings only through Sponsors; full map gives 7 appeal.

answers.answer: 1. Benefits gained earlier in an action, including money, cards, and newly activated workers, can be used for later steps in that action. Pay each item before receiving that item's own benefits; an animal's play-triggered money is paid only after its full cost. 2. Resolve ordinary effects immediately as they arise, including between animals or sequential buildings/tasks; ‘after finishing’ effects wait until the whole action and Action-card movement are complete. 3. If multiple effects are simultaneous, the owning player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: earlier action benefits may be used later and items resolve one at a time; animal money timing; after-finishing timing; simultaneous effects order.

answers.answer: 1. To play an animal, meet every printed condition, pay its cost, provide legal housing and terrain adjacency, place the card, then resolve its effects. A matching-continent partner zoo reduces its cost by 3 money per continent icon printed on the animal, including doubled icons. 2. A standard enclosure must be empty and at least the required size; put the animal there alone and flip the whole enclosure to its occupied side. Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo. 3. Eligible reptiles or birds may use a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary if its alternative icon applies and enough capacity remains; add one supply player token per indicated space and never flip the special enclosure. Special capacities are 3 for Petting Zoo and 5 each for Reptile House and Aviary. 4. The animal's required water/rock adjacency applies to whichever enclosure is chosen, including special enclosures. Count distinct adjacent terrain hexes; several touching edges to one terrain hex still count once. 5. Immediate effects resolve before the next animal; after-finishing effects wait until the Animals action and card movement are done. When playing two animals, finish the first's steps before the second.
answers.evidence: ANIMALS action: conditions, cost reduction per continent icon, standard/special housing and terrain; effect timing and two-animal sequence.

answers.answer: 1. Animals II lets you play eligible Animal cards from the display within reputation range as well as from hand; pay an extra cost equal to the card's folder number. 2. At strength 5+, you may gain 1 reputation at the very beginning of the action, before choosing animals, so the increased range can apply. 3. Display cards are not replenished until the turn ends. 4. Animals II also allows animals whose conditions show the upgrade-required icon.
answers.evidence: ANIMALS Side II: display play within range with folder-number cost; optional reputation first at strength 5+; display not replenished until turn ends; upgrade-required conditions allowed.

answers.answer: 1. Relocation is allowed only immediately when a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary is built, including through a permitted bonus. 2. You may move all eligible corresponding animals that fit, deciding separately for each; each moved animal must meet the new special enclosure's terrain adjacency and have enough free capacity. Add the animal's indicated number of supply player tokens to mark occupied spaces; never flip the special enclosure. 3. To free standard space, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all of that animal's requirements, including terrain. If none meets all requirements, flip the smallest occupied one meeting the animal's size requirement; if none meets size, flip none. 4. This relocates the existing animal; it is not a release. The summary does not specify a separate numeric maximum number of animals moved beyond all eligible animals that fit.
answers.evidence: Moving existing animals: only at special-enclosure construction; ‘all corresponding eligible animals that fit’; terrain/capacity; token marking and smallest-enclosure fallback.

answers.answer: 1. The four Association task strengths are reputation 2, partner zoo 3, university 4, and conservation project work 5. 2. Association I performs exactly one task; Association II performs one or more different tasks whose total task value is no more than action strength, then may make exactly one donation if at least one task was performed. 3. You need an active worker for each task. If one of your workers is already on that task, place 2 workers for the repeat; if 3 of yours are there, you cannot do it again until after the break. 4. Other players' workers on the task do not matter.
answers.evidence: ASSOCIATION action: task strengths; side-I and side-II limits; worker repetition rule; other players' workers do not matter.

answers.answer: 1. Take partner zoos and universities from the available tiles on the Association board and place them on the lowest empty corresponding space on your zoo map; resolve any printed covered-space bonus immediately. 2. A university's own reputation award is also resolved immediately; do not take duplicate universities. 3. Partner zoos must be from different continents, maximum four; the third and fourth require Association II. 4. A partner zoo reduces matching-continent animal costs by 3 per continent icon and provides that continent icon. 5. Universities provide research icons; only the hand-limit university raises the hand limit from 3 to 5. Other universities do not change the hand limit.
answers.evidence: ASSOCIATION tasks, University tiles, and zoo map: available board tiles, placement/bonuses, partner limits and university effects.

answers.answer: 1. Conservation project work may support a project already in play or play a project card from hand and support it immediately; with Association II, new project cards may instead come from the reputation-range display for a folder-number cost. Put a new card above the Association board at its leftmost space, shifting older cards right. 2. To support, fulfill a printed condition and choose an unoccupied reward level. A project may normally be supported only once by you, and a level is blocked by any player's token. 3. Take a player token from the left edge of your map and put it on the chosen condition; gain the printed conservation/reputation and activate the uncovered map bonus immediately, before or after the project reward. Recurring income repeats at breaks. 4. If a new project exceeds the player-count limit above the board, discard the rightmost project; tokens on it return to their owners' supplies, while their map bonuses remain activated. Base projects below the board never move or replenish.
answers.evidence: Association conservation project work: entering play, support limits/procedure, token source, bonus timing, overflow and base-project handling.

answers.answer: 1. A release project matches the animal's printed standard-enclosure requirement to the depicted size category: 2− is size 1 or 2, 3 is size 3, and 4+ is size 4 or 5; the actual enclosure tile or special-enclosure capacity does not determine the category. 2. Before gaining conservation, lose only that animal's printed appeal; discard it and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal, and earlier effects already earned. 3. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; later supporting it grants no such play bonus. 4. If the animal could use a special enclosure and its indicated special tokens can be removed, remove them; only otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements, or fallback to the smallest meeting size alone; if none meets size, flip none.
answers.evidence: Release into the wild projects: size bands; appeal/icon loss and retained effects; project play reputation; special-token and standard-enclosure release procedure.

answers.answer: 1. Sponsors I plays exactly 1 hand Sponsor if strength is at least its level and conditions are met, or advances the Break token by strength and takes that much money. 2. Sponsors II plays one or more Sponsors from hand and/or reputation-range display; action strength plus 1 must be at least the sum of levels. Pay each display card's folder number; replenish only at turn end. 3. Resolve cards one at a time, completing each card's immediate effects before the next and delaying after-finishing effects until the action ends. Sponsors II also permits upgrade-conditioned cards. 4. If choosing the money option, Sponsors II advances the Break token and takes twice the money. This remains the full amount even if fewer spaces remain before the last space; extra movement is ignored.
answers.evidence: SPONSORS action: I and II level limits/sources/cost/effect order; money option pays twice; break rules ignore excess steps.

answers.answer: 1. Break order: discard to hand limit; clear Multiplier, Venom, and Constriction tokens; recall workers and restock eligible partner-zoo/university tiles; discard display folders 1–2, compact and refill; take income; reset Break token. 2. Hand limit is normally 3 or 5 with the hand-limit university and is checked only at breaks. 3. Each kiosk earns 1 money for each adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, and pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not qualify. 4. If multiple players take display cards during break income, resolve them clockwise starting with the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise); refill the display after each such player's income before the next affected player chooses.
answers.evidence: Break procedure steps 1–6; kiosk income definition; display-card income ordering and between-player refill.

answers.answer: 1. At 2 conservation, each player chooses either an Action-card upgrade or an additional active association worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or an available Bonus tile. At 10, the first player to reach it makes all players discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile; if nobody reaches 10 before game end, all players discard one before scoring. 2. Check for game end at the end of your own turn or during a break when Appeal and Conservation are in the same scoring area or pass one another. Appeal gained during another player's turn waits until your own turn ends or a break unless another player triggers the end first. 3. If triggered at the end of a player's turn, the other players each take one more turn; if triggered during a break, all players take one more turn. 4. Each Final Scoring card is capped at 4 conservation. 5. VP equals your appeal minus the lowest appeal value in the scoring area of your Conservation counter. Highest positive VP wins; ties go to the player with most supported projects, then tied players share victory.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory: conservation milestone rewards, end trigger and timing, last turns, Final Scoring cap, VP formula and tiebreak.

answers.answer: 1. Shuffle the 9 Bonus tiles and place one random tile face up on each of the four blank yellow spaces beside Conservation track spaces 5 and 8: two tiles beside 5 and two beside 8. Do not place tiles on the two yellow spaces with icons; return the remaining 5 tiles to the box. 2. Components are not a hard limit: if a component runs out, use a suitable substitute. Explicit per-zoo limits and Association-board availability rules still apply.
answers.evidence: Global setup step 2; Component supply: use suitable substitute if a component runs out, while explicit limits remain.

answers.answer: 1. For advanced Maps 1–8, take two random zoo maps and choose one; alternatively lay out player count plus one advanced maps and choose one each in reverse play order. Return unselected maps to the box. 2. Map A begins with an empty 3-space enclosure and a kiosk on its indicated spaces; the printed kiosk is already built, with a tile placed over it as a reminder.
answers.evidence: Personal setup A: advanced-map selection methods; Map A ability starts with empty size-3 enclosure and kiosk.

answers.answer: 1. The seven player tokens used for conservation support begin on the designated spaces at the left edge of each zoo map. 2. When hiring a worker, activate the lowest remaining reserve worker first. 3. Certain maps award conservation points when you hire your last worker; the exact reward depends on the map and is not universal.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C2; Association worker supply: hire from lowest supply space upward; certain maps grant conservation for last worker.

answers.answer: 1. Flip one chosen Action card from side I to side II in its current slot; do not move it. 2. It counts as upgraded immediately for conditions, but its improved action is usable only from your next action; the action during which it upgraded retains the kind and strength set at its start. 3. There are four upgrade sources: Conservation track, Reputation track, second partner zoo, and second partner university. One source offers an alternative choice, so you cannot upgrade all five cards.
answers.evidence: Upgrading Action cards: stays in slot, immediate condition status, next-action capabilities; four ways and cannot upgrade all.

answers.answer: 1. At strength 1, Cards I draws 1 and discards 1; strength 2 draws 1 and discards 0; strength 3 draws 2 and discards 1; strength 4 draws 2 and discards 0; strength 5 or more draws 3 and discards 1. 2. A required discard may be a card just drawn or one already in your hand.
answers.evidence: Cards draw tables, Side I row; required discard may be newly drawn or previously held.

answers.answer: 1. Count bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear, and Petting Zoo animal as animal categories. Bear and Petting Zoo animal are special categories and are included unless explicitly excluded; bear may also appear alongside herbivore or predator.
answers.evidence: Animal categories and Base glossary shared principles list all seven and specify special cases.

answers.answer: 1. A donation is available only with Association II, after performing at least one Association task in the same action; it needs no worker and is limited to one per Association action. 2. Pay the smallest amount still visible in the donation area, cover that space with one of your supply player tokens, and gain 1 conservation point. 3. Printed costs are 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then a repeatable 12-money space. Skip spaces blocked at setup; after all spaces except the last are covered, later donations cost 12 and place no further token. The summary does not state any additional donation eligibility conditions.
answers.evidence: Association II donation: task requirement, no worker, once per action, smallest visible payment, token and conservation, cost ladder and repeat.

answers.answer: 1. Count upper-right icons on Animal and Sponsor cards; also count water/rock requirements in the upper-left on Animal cards and unique-building Sponsor cards. Count partner-zoo continent icons and university continent/research icons. 2. Do not count left-side play conditions or conservation-project icons; university reputation and hand-limit benefits are not zoo icons. 3. A card counts its own icons for effects and recurring triggers; doubled icons count twice, while repeated icons count only once when asked for different icon types. 4. Card text takes priority over general rules.
answers.evidence: Counting icons in your zoo; card-self and doubled-icon rules; ‘Card text takes priority over general rules.’

answers.answer: 1. Count distinct adjacent water or rock hexes; several edges touching the same terrain hex count as one, and a larger region counts only the hexes actually adjacent. Meet the animal's printed requirement for one or two such spaces. 2. Decorative water/rock illustrations on tiles are neither terrain spaces nor requirements.
answers.evidence: Animal housing terrain rules; Base glossary: terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes; illustrations on tiles are not terrain spaces.

answers.answer: 1. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; supporting a release project already in play does not grant that play bonus. 2. A Reptile Breeding Program has the same requirement for all three reward spaces; choose any available space whose reward level is unoccupied, subject to normal support rules.
answers.evidence: Release projects: new project grants reputation, later support does not; Breeding Program requirement same all spaces, choose any available space.

answers.answer: 1. In an effect written X : Y, X on the left is the condition and Y on the right is the reward. 2. A condition without a number, or phrased ‘per’, rewards once per fulfillment. 3. For numbered thresholds, reward only once and use the highest threshold met.
answers.evidence: Base glossary: shared principles for reading X:Y effects, conditions without numbers/per, and numbered thresholds.

answers.answer: 1. A connected space is uncovered and shares an edge with a covered space. 2. An isolated space has no adjacent covered space. 3. A border space lacks a neighboring map hex on at least one of its six sides. 4. ‘Your zoo’ includes your played cards, map, and personal supply; ‘any zoo’ includes those areas for all players.
answers.evidence: Base glossary definitions: connected, isolated, border space, your zoo and any zoo.

answers.answer: 1. Unique buildings enter play only through their Sponsor cards and must be placed when that Sponsor is played; if placement is impossible, the Sponsor cannot be played. 2. Use the matching tile colored-face up; rotate freely but do not flip it. Apply ordinary placement and any printed terrain-adjacency rules. 3. No size-based construction payment is due. Unique buildings are not enclosures, cannot house additional animals, and do not count as water or rock spaces.
answers.evidence: Base glossary unique buildings: placement, orientation, placement/terrain rules, no size-based payment, enclosure and terrain status.

answers.answer: 1. For either Named Action or Determination, finish the Animals action and move the Animals card to slot 1 before taking the granted action; use the granted action's Action card normally and move that card to slot 1 after it. 2. A Named Action requires the named action and cannot be replaced by the X-token alternative. 3. Determination (Any Action) permits any action, including the X-token alternative.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: shared timing/movement and Named Action versus Determination.

answers.answer: 1. Assertion or Dominance searches the unused face-down base-project deck and adds the chosen project (Assertion) or named project (Dominance) to hand. 2. Dominance has no effect if the named project is already in play. 3. Later play and immediately support the obtained card through Association, placing it above the board; it does not join the setup base-project row below.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Assertion/Dominance source, already-in-play exception, later play location.

answers.answer: 1. Resolve Boost or Clever after finishing Animals and moving that Action card. 2. Clever places the chosen card in slot 1; cards formerly left of it shift right. 3. Boost places the named card in slot 1 or slot 5; moving it to slot 5 shifts cards formerly to its right left.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Boost/Clever timing and card movement.

answers.answer: 1. Venom, Hypnosis, Pilfering, and Constriction target eligibility requires the affected zoo to have at least 5 appeal. The playing animal's appeal may be awarded before or after its interactive ability; normally its new appeal need not count when choosing affected players. 2. Interactive abilities may be replaced by the alternative text marked for solo if the multiplayer group prefers; playing solo mode is not required.
answers.evidence: Interactive abilities: all affected zoos need at least 5 appeal; playing animal appeal timing; multiplayer group may use solo alternative text.

answers.answer: 1. A target ahead of you on only one of Appeal or Conservation receives one Constriction token on its slot-5 card; a target ahead on both receives two, on slots 4 and 5. Affected zoos must have at least 5 appeal. 2. Never stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates. 3. A constricted action loses 2 strength, including each execution of a multiplied action; X-tokens may restore strength. 4. Return the token after the action, or at the break without effect.
answers.evidence: Interactive abilities table and Constriction rules: eligibility, token placement/count, strength loss, multiplied actions and removal.

answers.answer: 1. A Constriction token reduces the affected action by 2 strength. At effective strength zero or below, the player must spend enough X-tokens to reach at least 1, use the alternative X-token action, or leave the card unused until it is at least in slot 3. 2. The summary does not separately state that taking the alternative X-token action removes a Constriction token; general Constriction rules say return it after acting or at break without effect.
answers.evidence: Constriction: at strength zero or below, use enough X-tokens, use alternative X-token action, or leave card until slot 3; return token after acting or at break.

answers.answer: 1. Digging lets you choose again after each card; you may change between the two options for its up-to-two selections. 2. Discarding a display card through Digging replenishes it immediately, shifting higher folders down and drawing into folder 6.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Digging 2 options; decide again after each; display replacement is immediate.

answers.answer: 1. A flock animal may avoid flipping/occupying a new enclosure if another herbivore in your zoo requires at least the flock animal's standard-enclosure size. 2. The same qualifying herbivore can host any number of flock animals and need not itself be a flock animal. 3. Without such a host, house it normally; a later non-flock herbivore cannot join it in that enclosure. 4. When releasing a flock animal, follow the normal release/fallback procedure even if it originally shared; exact historical residents are not tracked.
answers.evidence: Flock Animal clarification: qualifying host, reuse, later non-flock animal, release procedure and no historical tracking.

answers.answer: 1. Full-throated activates the lowest remaining reserve worker by moving it to the notepad for immediate use. 2. If hiring that worker is your last worker, take any conservation-point reward printed on your map for hiring the last worker. 3. If all workers are already active, Full-throated has no effect.
answers.evidence: Full-throated clarification: activate lowest reserve worker, map reward for last worker, no effect if all active.

answers.answer: 1. Hunter reveals the stated number of deck cards, keeps one revealed Animal card, and discards all other revealed cards. If none is an Animal, discard all revealed cards and add nothing to hand.
answers.evidence: Hunter X clarification: keep one Animal; with no Animal among revealed cards, discard all.

answers.answer: 1. Hypnosis targets a zoo tied for highest appeal with at least 5 appeal; choose among ties. If you are the target, it has no effect. 2. Copy only a card in target slot 1, 2, or 3. Use that card's owner's upgraded or unupgraded side for the whole action, but use your own X-tokens and your own other-action upgrade checks. 3. Venom and Constriction on the copied card affect you and are discarded afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used. Move the targeted Action card to slot 1 normally after its use.
answers.evidence: Hypnosis clarification: highest-appeal eligibility/ties/self, slots and side; own X-tokens; copied-card tokens; move card normally.

answers.answer: 1. Put a gained Multiplier on the Action card named by its reward; if gained from a Bonus tile, choose any of your Action cards, including Animals. 2. On its next use, the action may be executed twice in succession at the same base strength; move the Action card only after both executions. Each X-token boosts only one execution. 3. Defer after-finishing effects until both executions are complete. A break triggered by the first execution waits until the whole turn is finished; it does not stop the second. 4. Return used Multiplier tokens to supply; remove unused tokens at the next break.
answers.evidence: Multiplier rules: token placement, two executions, X-token use, after-finishing timing, break timing and return.

answers.answer: 1. Each additional Multiplier adds one execution; two Multiplier tokens permit up to three actions, not four. 2. You may choose different permitted options in each regular execution. A multiplied X-token alternative can take two X-tokens, subject to the five-token cap, but cannot combine one X-token action with one regular action.
answers.evidence: Multiplier: additional tokens, choices per execution, multiplied X-token alternative and no mixed regular/X-token executions.

answers.answer: 1. Peacocking permits placing the Large Bird Aviary before upgrading Build, provided your zoo has no Aviary yet and a legal site exists. 2. Other placement restrictions remain, including Build II for restricted-icon map spaces. 3. Peacocking and Posturing placements follow normal placement rules, including kiosk spacing, and multiple buildings are placed one at a time.
answers.evidence: Peacocking: may build Aviary before Build upgrade, no existing Aviary, legal site; other restrictions remain. Posturing: normal rules and sequential placement.

answers.answer: 1. The first Petting Zoo animal grants 3 appeal, the second 6, and the third 9. 2. A single Petting Zoo can hold at most 3 such animals. 3. Petting Zoo animals count as small animals.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarification: Petting Zoo animal rewards, capacity and small-animal status.

answers.answer: 1. Pilfering 1 targets a zoo tied for highest appeal with at least 5 appeal; choose among tied leaders. 2. Pilfering 2 separately selects a highest-appeal target and a most-conservation target, each with at least 5 appeal; a conservation target must have at least 1 conservation. Choose ties. If one player leads both, target that player twice. If all players have zero conservation, the conservation-target part has no effect, while the highest-appeal part still resolves. 3. Self-targeting has no effect.
answers.evidence: Pilfering X clarification: targets, eligibility, ties, same target twice, all-zero conservation exception and self-target.

answers.answer: 1. The target chooses whether to give 5 money or allow a random hand-card draw; Final Scoring cards are never drawn. 2. If the target has no hand cards, they give 5 money; if they have less than 5 money, they give a card. If they have neither a card nor 5 money, they give all current money, including zero. 3. Resolve repeated pilferings sequentially, and the target may make a different choice each time.
answers.evidence: Pilfering X: target's choice, hand-card restriction, low/no-resource exceptions and sequential resolution.

answers.answer: 1. Cards tucked under an animal by Pouch have no remaining function. If that animal is released, discard its tucked cards too, but retain the appeal already earned for tucking them. 2. Cards sold through Sunbathing go to the discard pile; each sold card yields 4 money, up to the ability's X limit.
answers.evidence: Pouch X and Sunbathing X clarifications: tucked-card status/release and sale/discard handling.

answers.answer: 1. An extra Final Scoring card from Resistance drawn before the 10-conservation milestone joins the player's choices when they discard one card at that milestone. 2. At game end, score every remaining Final Scoring card; each is individually capped at 4 conservation points.
answers.evidence: Resistance clarification; Final Scoring rules cap each individual card at 4.

answers.answer: 1. Shuffle the discard pile face down, draw randomly from it, apply the Scavenging card's stated selection, and then return the discard pile face up. For the illustrated Scavenging 3, draw 3 random cards, keep 1, and discard the other 2.
answers.evidence: Scavenging clarification: shuffle face down, draw randomly, select, return face up; Scavenging 3 example.

answers.answer: 1. Snapping takes exactly one display card regardless of reputation; it does not let you draw from the deck instead. 2. Sponsor Magnet looks only for display Sponsor cards, which need not be within reputation range; if none is present, nothing happens. 3. Ordinary end-of-turn display refill applies.
answers.evidence: Snapping/Sponsor Magnet clarification: card source, range, empty result and ordinary refill.

answers.answer: 1. Venom tokens affect every other zoo with higher appeal than yours and at least 5 appeal; put them on cards in the lowest slots first (1, then 2, etc.), at most one per card, returning duplicates. 2. Using a marked card removes its token and avoids all Venom fees for that turn; the X-token alternative also counts if you hold fewer than 5 X-tokens. 3. At turn end, pay 2 money only if you removed no Venom token that turn and at least one remains on your cards. If unable, undo the turn and choose another action; spending all money cannot avoid the fee. 4. Unused tokens clear at the next break without effect.
answers.evidence: Venom clarification: eligible targets and token placement; use/removal; turn-end fee and inability exception; break expiry.

answers.answer: 1. Veterinarian's immediate reward is 2/5/10 money for having 1/2/3 universities. 2. It lowers the strength needed for conservation-project support from 5 to 4. 3. Its final reward is 1 conservation for three universities.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 203 Veterinarian: immediate, recurring permission, final scoring.

answers.answer: 1. Medical Breakthrough's immediate appeal is 2 per previously supported project, counted by the player tokens missing from the left edge of the zoo map. 2. It gives 1 conservation at each break.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 206 Medical Breakthrough: immediate count and break income.

answers.answer: 1. Basic Research totals distinct continent and animal-category icon types together, counting each type only once even if repeated or doubled; research icons are excluded. Gain 1 conservation per 2 types, rounding down. 2. Every other player gains 2 money per conservation point you gain.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 207 Basic Research: distinct icon types, excluded research, reward and opponent money.

answers.answer: 1. Science Library gains 1 appeal per research icon when played. 2. Whenever any player plays a research icon, the Science Library owner gains 2 money. 3. Its final reward is 1 conservation with five different animal categories.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 208 Science Library: I, recurring trigger, final condition.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on the Americas gives 1 appeal per Americas icon when played. 2. Each Americas icon later played permits a free kiosk, following normal placement and spacing rules. 3. Its final reward is 1 conservation with five or more kiosks.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 210 Expert on the Americas: immediate icon appeal, free kiosk rules, final condition.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on Australia gives 1 appeal per Australia icon when played. 2. For each Australia icon played, you may tuck one hand card beneath this Sponsor for 2 appeal. 3. Tucked cards have no further function. The summary does not state an additional disposition for those cards beyond that status.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 212 Expert on Australia: immediate and recurring effect; tucked cards have no further function.

answers.answer: 1. Each of Global Breeding Program and Breeding Program places two supply tokens on itself. When supporting a base project below the Association board, you may return exactly one token as any one icon; never use both on the same support. 2. Cards that originated as base projects but are later played above the board do not qualify. 3. The final reward is 1 conservation with five or more project supports, counted by missing left-map tokens.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 215/218: token substitute use, eligible base projects, final support count.

answers.answer: 1. Engineer lets each Build action add one extra copy of a building built in that same action without additional strength. 2. Pay the extra building's normal money cost and obey placement rules. Only one extra building is allowed even if the action builds several different buildings; special enclosures remain limited to one per type per zoo. 3. Its final reward is 5 appeal with a full map except water and rock.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 217 Engineer: extra-copy effect, payment and limits, final reward.

answers.answer: 1. Diversity Researcher gives 2 money per water/rock icon when played. 2. It permits covering water/rock spaces and ignoring terrain requirements of animals and unique buildings; printed terrain icons still count. Terrain need not be covered for a full-map reward. 3. Covered terrain no longer counts for Hydrologist, Geologist, or Architectural Zoo. 4. Its final reward is 2 appeal per water-icon/rock-icon pair, maximum 3 pairs.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 219 Diversity Researcher: immediate money, terrain permissions/counting, final scoring.

answers.answer: 1. Archaeologist triggers when an actual placement bonus on a border space is gained. 2. For each such bonus, it grants one extra choice of any uncovered placement bonus on your map, not necessarily on a border; multiple triggers can choose the same or different bonuses. Resolve bonuses in the order you choose. 3. Its final reward is 1 conservation when all building border spaces are covered, excluding water/rock.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 221 Archaeologist: trigger, extra choice, repeated choice/order, final condition.

answers.answer: 1. Migration Recording gives 1 X-token when played. 2. Each Release into the Wild support gives 1 additional conservation. You may support the same release project repeatedly with different qualifying animals, but place at most one token on that project per Association action. 3. Each placed token counts as a separate project support for other effects.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 224 Migration Recording: immediate reward and release-support modifications.

answers.answer: 1. Quarantine Lab gives 1 X-token when played. 2. It makes you immune to Venom, Constriction, Hypnosis, and Pilfering. For Hypnosis and Pilfering, ignore your counters and select the next qualifying player. 3. Its final reward is 1 conservation with all five continents.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 225 Quarantine Lab: immediate reward, immunities/redirect, final condition.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Special Assignment permanently chooses either small or large animals and marks that choice with a player token from your supply. Reveal deck cards until finding an animal of that type; keep it and discard the other revealed cards. 2. Thereafter, you cannot play the opposite type. 3. Chosen small animals gain 2 extra appeal; chosen large animals gain 4 extra appeal. Size-3 animals remain legal but get no bonus.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 227 WAZA Special Assignment: choice, search, prohibition and size-specific bonuses.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Small Animals Program gives 2 money per small animal when played. 2. If an Animals action contains only small animals, you may play one additional small animal from hand with normal costs and rules; mixing small and large in the original action prevents this. 3. Then you may add one small Animal card from the display to hand regardless of reputation, even if you declined the extra play. The summary does not specify a separate folder cost for this card-taking effect.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 228: immediate money; all-small action condition and extra hand animal; display card regardless of reputation.

answers.answer: 1. Hydrologist gives 1 appeal per water icon when played. 2. Its recurring effect gives 1 money for each newly covered space adjacent to water, even when several spaces are part of one building; a space adjacent to several water hexes pays only once. 3. Its final reward is 1 conservation if all water hexes are connected, meaning none is isolated.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 241 Hydrologist: immediate, newly covered space money rule, final condition.

answers.answer: 1. Barred Owl Hut places its unique building in the zoo, subject to its placement rules. 2. Each bird icon played triggers drawing two deck cards, keeping one and discarding the other. The card's own icon may trigger its effect.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 249; Sponsor card effect principle says the card counts its own icon.

answers.answer: 1. Place Sea Turtle Tank adjacent to water. 2. Each reptile icon played lets you sell up to two hand cards for 4 money each; sold cards go to the discard pile. The card's own icon counts for its effect.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 250 Sea Turtle Tank; effects count card's own icons.

answers.answer: 1. Place Spotted Hyena Compound in your zoo. Each predator icon played triggers Hunter with a number of draws equal to your total predator icons. 2. A card with a double-predator icon triggers two Hunters sequentially; count the newly added icons for the second Hunter as well.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 252 Spotted Hyena Compound: Hunter amount and sequential duplicate-icon rule.

answers.answer: 1. Place Okapi Stable with three supply tokens on its card. For each herbivore icon played, you may spend one token and pay money equal to a hand Sponsor's level to play that Sponsor, subject to its usual conditions. 2. The Stable's own herbivore icon may trigger this when it is played. It can be used three times total. 3. The Sponsor must come from hand; the summary specifies a hand Sponsor, even if Sponsors is upgraded.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 253 Okapi Stable: tokens, per-icon use, level cost, conditions, self-trigger, three uses; general FAQ specifies hand source for paid-Sponsor effects.

answers.answer: 1. Zoo School gives 1 reputation and 1 conservation. 2. Place its unique building so that it covers at least two border spaces. 3. Take one display card within reputation range or draw one deck card. Resolve its simultaneous benefits in an order you choose.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 254 Zoo School: track rewards, placement and card options/order.

answers.answer: 1. Side Entrance is a unique building placed on two border spaces; it need not touch an existing building, though other placement rules apply. 2. Later buildings may attach to it. 3. At each break it gives 2 money per adjacent building except empty standard enclosures; it may be adjacent to a kiosk. As a unique building, it counts for kiosk income. 4. Its final reward is 5 appeal with a full map excluding water/rock.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 257 Side Entrance: placement exception, adjacency, break income/kiosk status, final reward.

answers.answer: 1. Native Farm Animals gives 1 appeal per connected, uncovered building border space; water and rock spaces are excluded. 2. At game end, gain 1 conservation per six contiguous empty building spaces; evaluate each group separately and sum the completed groups. The summary's example groups of 13, 6, 3, and 2 spaces score 2+1+0+0=3. 3. Restricted spaces count even if Build is not upgraded; terrain spaces do not count.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 260 Native Farm Animals: immediate spaces, end groups/example, restricted and terrain handling.

answers.answer: 1. Explorer's immediate reward is 2 money per different continent or animal-category icon type; research icons are excluded. 2. Its recurring reward applies when a category or continent is newly introduced to your zoo: gain 1 appeal and 2 money per newly introduced type. A doubled copy of the same new icon grants that novelty benefit only once.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 262 Explorer: immediate icon counting and new-type benefit including duplicate icon rule.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Large Animal Program lets you place a size-5 standard enclosure for free under normal placement rules. 2. When playing a large animal, ignore one left-side condition, such as one required icon or the Animals upgrade; terrain requirements cannot be ignored. 3. It stacks with Research Institute, allowing two conditions to be ignored.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 263 WAZA Large Animal Program: free enclosure, one condition waiver, terrain exception and stacking.

answers.answer: 1. Biodiverse Zoo compares each animal category's icon count in your zoo with the player to your right; gain 1 conservation for each category where your count is higher. 2. If that player has no icons in a category, one of yours is enough to exceed them. 3. Maximum reward is 4 conservation.
answers.evidence: Base Final Scoring and map clarifications: Biodiverse Zoo comparison, zero-count case and cap.

answers.answer: 1. Observation Tower's bonus applies only to standard enclosures adjacent to the tower hex itself, not merely another rock hex. 2. Special enclosures do not qualify. 3. Housing an animal there grants the two appeal again after an earlier animal was released. 4. The tower is not a building for kiosk income.
answers.evidence: Map 1 Observation Tower clarification: qualifying adjacency, repeat after release, special enclosure and building status.

answers.answer: 1. Outdoor Areas qualifies a standard enclosure that touches the Outdoor Area hex itself, not merely another water hex. 2. Such an enclosure counts as two spaces larger for all purposes after placement; a physical size-2 enclosure there is treated as size 4. 3. You cannot ignore this for release or transfer. 4. It does not affect special enclosures, and the Outdoor Area is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 2 Outdoor Areas clarification: adjacency, size treatment, release/transfer and special-enclosure/building exceptions.

answers.answer: 1. Commercial Harbor is activated by placing a building on its adjacent building space; your first building may start next to the Harbor but does not have to. 2. Its discard ability may be used before, during, or after your action, once per your own turn, never during breaks or another player's turn. 3. The Harbor is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 4 Commercial Harbor clarification: activation, first building, timing/limit and status.

answers.answer: 1. Park Restaurant income is 1 money per adjacent covered hex, regardless of building type, occupancy, or how many spaces belong to one building; empty enclosures therefore qualify if covered. 2. The Restaurant itself is not a building and does not count as a kiosk neighbor. 3. Its special-enclosure placement bonus gives one free Reptile House or one free Large Bird Aviary, even before Build II; choose one, not both, and obey all other normal placement rules.
answers.evidence: Map 5 Park Restaurant clarification: income per hex and covered status, Restaurant type, free special-enclosure choice and restrictions.

answers.answer: 1. Cover each Hollywood Hills H space with a building under ordinary placement rules. When an H is covered, reveal deck cards until a Sponsor appears, keep it, and discard the others. 2. H is not a placement bonus and does not trigger Archaeologist. 3. After all three H spaces are covered, every Sponsor's level is reduced by 1. 4. Bonus partner zoos still require Association II for the third or fourth partner; bonus buildings still require Build II for restricted-icon spaces.
answers.evidence: Map 8 Hollywood Hills clarification: covering/reveal, no Archaeologist, all-three reward and persistent upgrade restrictions.

answers.answer: 1. For a bonus that lets you pay to play a Sponsor, pay money equal to the Sponsor's level and meet its usual conditions. 2. Play the card only from hand, even if Sponsors is upgraded; you cannot take it from the display for this bonus. 3. The Sponsors Action card stays in its current slot and does not move.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: paid-Sponsor bonus cost, normal conditions, hand-only source and Sponsors card position.

answers.answer: 1. Appeal cannot exceed 113; appeal gained beyond that end of track is lost. 2. Conservation cannot exceed 41; conservation gained beyond that end is lost.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: Appeal cannot exceed 113; conservation cannot exceed 41; excess gains are lost.

answers.answer: 1. Venom targets every other zoo with higher appeal than yours and at least 5 appeal. 2. Hypnosis targets a highest-appeal zoo with at least 5 appeal; choose among ties, and it has no effect if you are the target. It can copy only slots 1, 2, or 3. 3. Pilfering 1 targets a highest-appeal zoo with at least 5 appeal; Pilfering 2 separately targets the highest-appeal and most-conservation zoos, each requiring 5 appeal; a conservation target must have at least 1 conservation. Choose ties; self-targets have no effect; if the same zoo leads both tracks, Pilfering 2 targets it twice. 4. Constriction targets every other zoo with at least 5 appeal that is ahead of you on appeal and/or conservation; ahead on one track gets 1 token, ahead on both gets 2 tokens.
answers.evidence: Interactive ability target table and detailed Venom, Hypnosis, Pilfering, and Constriction rules.

answers.answer: 1. An Animal card's partner-zoo condition requires a partner zoo from the animal's continent. A Sponsor's partner-zoo condition permits a partner zoo from any continent. 2. A red maximum-25-appeal condition permits playing only while your zoo has 25 appeal or less; the marker at 25 is a reminder, not a general cap. 3. A minimum-reputation condition requires at least the printed reputation value. 4. An ignore-one-condition bonus removes one left-side requirement, such as a required icon or an upgrade requirement, but does not remove terrain requirements.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: partner conditions, max-25 appeal, minimum reputation and ignore-one-condition bonus.

answers.answer: 1. Digging 2 allows up to two selections, choosing each time between discarding a display card and replenishing it, or discarding a hand card and drawing one card from the deck. 2. Decide again after each card; the options may differ between selections.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarification: Digging 2 offers the two listed options, up to twice, deciding again after each.

answers.answer: 1. When display cards are replenished after a turn, move higher-numbered cards down into gaps while preserving their order, then fill remaining empty folders from the deck. 2. During a break, discard folders 1 and 2, move the remaining cards down, and refill. 3. If a Digging effect discards a display card, its replacement is immediate, shifting higher folders down and drawing into folder 6.
answers.evidence: Reputation track and display; break step 4; Digging clarification on immediate display replacement.

answers.answer: 1. Build standard enclosures empty side up, showing the yellow edge and size number. 2. Each placement-bonus space covered grants its bonus immediately, once; turning the enclosure occupied later does not award that placement bonus again.
answers.evidence: BUILD action: standard enclosure empty side up and placement bonuses once; covered space bonus is immediate.

answers.answer: 1. When the first player reaches or exceeds 10 conservation, all players choose and discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining Final Scoring pile. The summary specifies face down and under the pile; it does not specify a more exact orientation.
answers.evidence: Conservation track 10-point reward: all players discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile.

answers.answer: 1. Determine the starting player randomly; play proceeds clockwise, one turn at a time, without formal rounds. 2. On a turn, take one action using one of the five Action cards. Any additional action granted by an effect is resolved after the normal action as specified by that effect.
answers.evidence: Setup: randomly determine start player; turn order clockwise. Overview: no formal rounds; one turn at a time. Turn Structure: one action per turn.

answers.answer: 1. If no player reaches 10 conservation before the game ends, all players must discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring begins. The summary does not add a more specific orientation or destination for this fallback discard.
answers.evidence: Conservation track 10-point reward: if no one reaches 10 before game end, all players discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring begins.
